1.body: This repository implements Bazel rules for Terraform and OpenTofu .
1.title: Overview

10.body:
Both halves of a root module's external dependencies are declared on one tag, because that is how the engine treats them: terraform init installs the providers the lock pins and the registry modules the module blocks name in one step. The hub it produces, @<name>, is a terraform_dependency_group carrying both, and a terraform_module that depends on it needs no lock attribute. terraform = use_extension("@rules_terraform//terraform:extensions.bzl", "terraform")
terraform.deps( name = "my_deps", lock = "//path/to:.terraform.lock.hcl", # optional: providers roots = ["//path/to:main.tf"], # optional: registry modules # registry = "registry.opentofu.org", # default follows the extension
)
use_repo(terraform, "my_deps") Either half may be omitted: a shared library that names a registry module but no provider gets a tag with roots only. The parts are addressable too: @my_deps//:providers, @my_deps//:modules, and @my_deps//<namespace>_<name> for one provider.

16.body: The state of each bzlmod extension in rules_terraform: Extension Reproducible? Why terraform_toolchains / tofu_toolchains ✓ Every URL + integrity is vendored in //<engine>/private:versions.bzl. No network at eval time; identical inputs → identical repo declarations. deps tag, lock half ✓ Reads a checked-in .terraform.lock.hcl; never resolves version constraints. Registry API is called to look up download URLs, but the version and hash come from the lock. deps tag, roots half ✗ Live version-constraint resolution against the Registry API. MODULE.bazel.lock is the capture layer that closes the gap — see below.
16.title: Reproducibility

17.body:
The modules extension is the only piece of rules_terraform that depends on MODULE.bazel.lock for both reproducibility AND performance. terraform_toolchains, tofu_toolchains, and the lock half of a deps tag all read fully vendored state and produce deterministic output without any lockfile involvement. The modules extension is different in two related ways: Reproducibility. Without the lockfile, ~> 5.0 can resolve to 5.7.1 today and 5.7.2 tomorrow. With the lockfile enabled, bzlmod captures the extension's resolved output and reuses it on every subsequent eval — the extension is reproducible = False under Bazel's contract, but the lockfile makes builds byte-identical across time in practice. Performance. Every .tf edit invalidates the extension (bzlmod tracks each module_ctx.read()). Without any cache, every re-eval hits the Registry API three times per module block, including downloading each archive to compute an sha256 — MB per module. The extension caches per-(source, version) archive URL + integrity in module_ctx.facts; those facts persist through MODULE.bazel.lock. Without the lockfile, facts is always empty, and every re-eval pays the full cost. Recommended downstream setup — in your consuming repo's .bazelrc: common --lockfile_mode=update
# or, once you're confident in the state:
common --lockfile_mode=strict Commit MODULE.bazel.lock. This gives you: Deterministic builds regardless of version constraints in .tf. Cheap re-evals — cached facts short-circuit metadata calls and archive downloads on every re-run. A PR-visible diff (MODULE.bazel.lock) whenever a module version or archive hash actually changes. Bonus: pin exact versions in module { } blocks. Combined with MODULE.bazel.lock, exact pins let the extension skip even the /versions API call — bringing warm-cache re-evals to zero network calls per module: module "vpc" { source = "terraform-aws-modules/vpc/aws" version = "5.7.1" # not "~> 5.0"
}
17.title: The role of MODULE.bazel.lock

18.body: The ruleset commits its lockfile. Its own test fixtures use the modules extension, so the lockfile is what keeps bazel test //... here offline and repeatable, and a PR that bumps a fixture's module version shows the resolved archive in the diff. The examples under examples/ run with --lockfile_mode=off on purpose: they stand in for a downstream user's first build, where no facts exist yet.
18.title: Rules_terraform's own MODULE.bazel.lock

19.body: To bump a module version with the lockfile enabled: Edit the exact version (or constraint) in the module { } block. Run bazel mod deps --lockfile_mode=update (or just bazel fetch //...) to regenerate MODULE.bazel.lock. Commit both the .tf change AND the lockfile diff — reviewers see exactly which archive changed.
19.title: Update workflow

2.body:
Add rules_terraform to your MODULE.bazel: bazel_dep(name = "rules_terraform", version = "{version}") Toolchains for both engines are auto-registered — no use_extension or register_toolchains call is required. By default a build uses the newest release shipped in //terraform/private:versions.bzl / //tofu/private:versions.bzl ; those tables carry the three newest releases of each engine. Any other release is one tag away. The extension fetches that release's SHA256SUMS once and records the checksums as facts in MODULE.bazel.lock, so pinning an older engine needs no change to rules_terraform: terraform_toolchains = use_extension("@rules_terraform//terraform:extensions.bzl", "terraform_toolchains")
terraform_toolchains.version(version = "1.9.8", default = True) # default = True: use it unless the flag says otherwise tofu_toolchains = use_extension("@rules_terraform//tofu:extensions.bzl", "tofu_toolchains")
tofu_toolchains.version(version = "1.9.1") # available, selected by flag The flags select among the releases the hub knows, shipped or tagged: --@rules_terraform//terraform/settings:version=1.9.8
--@rules_terraform//tofu/settings:version=1.9.1 Left empty they mean "the default": the root module's default = True tag, else the newest shipped release. Nothing has to be installed on the host: the engine binary, provider archives and registry modules are all fetched by Bazel, and every bazel run / bazel test below uses the toolchain-fetched engine.
2.title: Setup

20.body: The extension makes live Registry API calls at eval time. Network responses CAN vary across invocations (transient 5xx, mirror rotation, registry outages, schema changes over years). Claiming reproducible = True would be dishonest — same inputs, potentially different outputs. MODULE.bazel.lock is Bazel's designed capture layer for exactly this shape of extension, and setting reproducible = True would tell bzlmod NOT to record the extension in the lockfile — the opposite of what we want.
20.breadcrumbs: Introduction » Why not just mark the extension reproducible = True?
20.title: Why not just mark the extension reproducible = True?

21.body: If HashiCorp publishes a Terraform-level module lockfile schema that captures resolved versions + hashes ahead of extension eval. If rules_terraform introduces a mode where the extension consumes a user-supplied pinned-version list without hitting the network at all (essentially reintroducing a lockfile — the one we deliberately removed in favor of live resolution + facts caching). Neither is planned. Until then, MODULE.bazel.lock + exact pins covers the same ground with Bazel's native machinery.
21.breadcrumbs: Introduction » When could reproducible = True come back?
21.title: When could reproducible = True come back?

23.body: terraform_binary — bazel run wrapper for any terraform subcommand. terraform_module — declares a .tf module with providers and deps. terraform_external_module — supplies a module fetched from outside the workspace (git, private hosts) to deps. terraform_provider — declares a provider built in the repo. Registry providers come from a deps tag's hub instead. terraform_test — runs Terraform's HCL native test framework, reporting each run block as a JUnit test case. terraform_plan_test — runs a real plan and keeps it as a reviewable test output; needs network. terraform_validate_test / aspect — terraform validate as a Bazel test/aspect. terraform_fmt_test / aspect — terraform fmt -check as a Bazel test/aspect. terraform_providers_lock — bazel run updater that writes .terraform.lock.hcl with the toolchain engine; nothing needs installing on the host. terraform_providers_lock_test — fails when the lock file and the required_providers blocks disagree.

28.body: load("@rules_terraform//terraform:terraform_external_module.bzl", "terraform_external_module") terraform_external_module(name, srcs, source, version) A module whose files come from outside the workspace. The terraform.modules(...) extension declares one of these per registry module it resolves. Declare one yourself, in the build_file_content of an http_archive or git_repository, to supply a module the extension cannot fetch: a module hosted somewhere other than a public registry, or a plain git:: / https:// source. Match source to the module block verbatim and list the target in the consuming terraform_module's deps. ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this target. Name required srcs Module source files. List of labels optional [] source The source string exactly as module blocks write it: a registry address (terraform-aws-modules/vpc/aws, with any //subdir), or any other address Terraform accepts, such as git::https://…?ref=v1.2.0. The init aspect installs this module under every module block whose source matches. String required version Module version. String required

34.body: load("@rules_terraform//terraform:terraform_module.bzl", "terraform_module") terraform_module(name, deps, srcs, data, allow_ephemeral_state, lock) Defines a Terraform module that can be used as a dependency in other Terraform targets. ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this target. Name required deps Other terraform_module targets, a dependency hub (@<name> from a deps tag, or its //:providers / //:modules halves), individual @<name>//<namespace>_<name> providers, terraform_provider, or terraform_external_module targets this module depends on.A terraform_module dep is the Bazel half of a module block, the way a py_library dep is the Bazel half of an import: the .tf file names the path, deps says which target supplies it. A dep whose package already nests under this module's directory lands at that relative path; anything else is matched to a module block whose source ends with the dep's package name. List of labels optional [] srcs Terraform source files that make up this module: .tf, .tf.json, and OpenTofu's .tofu / .tofu.json.All of them must live directly in this target's package — a Terraform module is a single directory. Put nested .tf files in their own terraform_module and reference it with a module block. List of labels optional [] data Additional files or targets that should be available at runtime. List of labels optional [] allow_ephemeral_state Permit bazel run of apply, destroy and the other state-writing commands against a module with no backend or cloud block.Without a backend the engine keeps state in its working directory, which under Bazel is a staged copy that exists for one run. The runner therefore refuses those commands by default, naming the fix. With this set, state is kept under bazel-out between runs: private to the machine, forked per build configuration, and deleted by bazel clean. Set it only where losing the state is harmless: demos, sandboxes, or bootstrapping the bucket that will hold real state. Ignored when a backend is declared; plan and the read-only commands are never gated. Boolean optional False lock An optional .terraform.lock.hcl file. Label optional None
34.title: terraform_module

36.body: load("@rules_terraform//terraform:terraform_plan_test.bzl", "terraform_plan_test") terraform_plan_test(name, tags, **kwargs) Runs a real terraform plan as a test and keeps the plan for review. A thin wrapper over the rule of the same name that adds the requires-network tag: a plan reaches the state backend and, for most providers, the provider's API. Credentials come from the environment, so pass them with --test_env. Providers that work offline (null, local, random) need neither. See the rule's documentation for the attributes and the artefacts left in the undeclared test outputs directory. PARAMETERS Name Description Default Value name (str) Target name. none tags (list[str]) Extra tags. requires-network is always added. [] kwargs Forwarded to the rule: root, plan_args, expect_no_changes, lock, and the usual test attributes. none

4.body:
rules_terraform ships two hub repositories — @terraform and @tofu — that let a user invoke the toolchain-resolved engine binary from any subdirectory of their workspace: cd path/to/my/tf/module
bazel run @terraform -- plan # ≈ terraform plan
bazel run @terraform -- init # ≈ terraform init
bazel run @tofu -- state list # ≈ tofu state list The wrapper chdirs to $BUILD_WORKING_DIRECTORY (the shell cwd where bazel run was invoked) before exec-ing the engine, so relative paths and any terraform.tfstate land in the directory you're standing in — just like the native CLI. Version resolution follows the same //terraform/settings:version / //tofu/settings:version flags as the rest of the ruleset, so you get one hermetic Terraform release across all invocations. It is also how a Terraform maintainer manages dependencies without touching Bazel: bazel run @terraform -- init -upgrade or bazel run @terraform -- providers lock in a module directory writes the lock the rules consume, and a module that depends on its providers hub as a whole (deps = ["@my_deps"]) picks the change up with no BUILD edit. To reformat sources, bazel run @rules_terraform//terraform:format (or //tofu:format) rewrites the .tf files of every module in the workspace with the toolchain engine's fmt; pass target patterns to narrow it. Modules tagged no_format or no_terraform_format are skipped, matching the fmt aspect. This is NOT the Bazel-managed workflow. @terraform does no init aspect, no lock-file rewriting, no .terraform construction — terraform init still runs against your source tree, hits the network, and writes state. Reach for it when you want a one-off CLI invocation (state manipulation, ad-hoc plan against an unrelated module) without wiring up a terraform_binary target for the module. To use @terraform / @tofu from downstream, add them to your MODULE.bazel: terraform_toolchains = use_extension("@rules_terraform//terraform:extensions.bzl", "terraform_toolchains")
use_repo(terraform_toolchains, "terraform") tofu_toolchains = use_extension("@rules_terraform//tofu:extensions.bzl", "tofu_toolchains")
use_repo(tofu_toolchains, "tofu") The extensions themselves are already invoked by rules_terraform's own MODULE.bazel (they register toolchains); the use_repo line only binds the repo name in your namespace so @terraform / @tofu resolve.

44.body: load("@rules_terraform//terraform:terraform_test.bzl", "terraform_test") terraform_test(name, root) Runs terraform's native HCL test framework (terraform test) on the root module as a Bazel test. Test cases live in .tftest.hcl files. Fully hermetic — the .terraform directory is assembled by the init aspect from Bazel-managed deps. Each run block is reported as a JUnit test case through Bazel's XML_OUTPUT_FILE (Terraform writes the report itself; for OpenTofu the runner builds it from the -json-into event stream, which is also kept). The lock file and module manifest the test ran against are saved as undeclared test outputs. Bazel --test_arg values are intentionally ignored so the surface stays predictable — every run executes the module's .tftest.hcl files. ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this target. Name required root The terraform_module target that serves as the root module. Label required

5.body: When a terraform_module is built through Bazel, an init aspect assembles the whole module directory hermetically — the directory the engine will run in, .tf files and .terraform/ alike — rather than letting terraform init build it. The result is a single Bazel tree artifact that terraform_binary and the validate rules copy and cd into. Every network fetch happens at repository-rule / bzlmod-extension time; build actions are offline. As a consequence: Provider binaries are fetched at repository-rule time and copied into .terraform/providers/… during the aspect's action. The lock file's h1: hashes are rewritten to match the actually-installed binary layout. External modules (from a Terraform registry) are resolved via a Bazel-owned lock file, downloaded at repository-rule time, and copied into .terraform/modules/… with a generated modules.json manifest. Local child modules — other terraform_module targets in the monorepo — are placed at the relative source path the parent's module block names, so Terraform resolves them the way it resolves any local module. Packages nested under the parent land there automatically; anything else is matched to the module block whose source names it. A terraform_module is exactly one directory: every file in srcs must live directly in the target's own package. Nested .tf files are a child module and belong in their own terraform_module. This is enforced at analysis time, and it is what lets the aspect know which directory it is building without guessing. The full mechanics — how the extensions resolve each dependency type, what each lock file looks like, and how to keep them fresh — are in External dependencies and lock files below.
5.title: Bazel-managed Terraform

50.body:
Materializes one hub repo (@terraform_toolchains) that declares a toolchain per (version, platform) for the releases shipped in //terraform/private:versions.bzl — the three newest when the table was generated — and for any release a version tag asks for. For a tagged release the extension fetches that release's SHA256SUMS once and records the checksums as facts in MODULE.bazel.lock. rules_terraform's own MODULE.bazel use_repos the hub and register_toolchainss it, so downstream users get toolchain resolution for free. Per-(version, platform) http_archives are lazy; only the selected combination is fetched. # Nothing to do beyond `bazel_dep` to use the newest shipped release.
bazel_dep(name = "rules_terraform", version = "...") # To use another release:
terraform_toolchains = use_extension("@rules_terraform//terraform:extensions.bzl", "terraform_toolchains")
terraform_toolchains.version(version = "1.9.8", default = True) terraform_toolchains.version Attribute Type Description version string (required) The release, e.g. 1.9.8. Shipped releases need no tag. default bool (default False) Use this release when //terraform/settings:version is empty. Root module only; at most one tag may set it. The hub declares a config_setting per known release, so the flag can select any of them: --@rules_terraform//terraform/settings:version=1.9.8.
50.title: terraform_toolchains

51.title: terraform

52.body: Public build settings for //terraform. Each exported function is named after a build setting in this package and its docstring describes what the setting does. The function body returns the setting's label so callers can reference it programmatically. Picks which Terraform release the auto-registered toolchains resolve to. The terraform_toolchains extension declares one toolchain per (version, platform) for the releases shipped in //terraform/private:versions.bzl — the newest three when the table was generated — and for any release a terraform_toolchains.version(version = "…") tag asks for. For a tagged release the extension fetches the release's SHA256SUMS once and records the checksums as facts in MODULE.bazel.lock, so an older pin costs no change to rules_terraform and no network on later evaluations. Empty, the default, selects the extension's default: the release the root module marked version(…, default = True), else the newest shipped one. Any other value names one of the known releases. Set it globally in .bazelrc, per invocation via --@rules_terraform//terraform/settings:version=1.9.8, or per target with a Starlark configuration transition. The corresponding archive is fetched lazily on first use.
52.title: version

53.body: Everything under //tofu mirrors //terraform but binds to //tofu:toolchain_type. Rule bodies are identical — only the resolved toolchain differs — so behavior stays in lockstep between the two engines. Data-only rules (tofu_module, tofu_external_module, tofu_provider, tofu_provider_group) are literal aliases for their terraform_* counterparts, provided so an OpenTofu-only project never has to import a terraform_* symbol.

6.body:
Once a terraform_module has Bazel-managed dependencies, running terraform (or tofu) directly outside Bazel is not expected to work : the module directory is Bazel's construction, h1: hashes are rewritten for the installed platform binary, and modules.json reflects the Bazel target graph — not the source tree. Use bazel run to invoke the engine: # Instead of: terraform plan
bazel run //path/to:terraform -- plan # Instead of: terraform apply
bazel run //path/to:terraform -- apply The terraform_binary rule creates an executable that copies the aspect-built module directory into a writable temp dir and runs the real terraform binary there. That temp dir is removed when the command finishes, which means a Bazel-run module needs a remote backend . Without a backend or cloud block, the runner refuses apply, destroy, import, refresh, taint, untaint and the writing state subcommands, and the message names the fix. plan and the read-only commands are never refused. Where disposable state is the point (demos, sandboxes, bootstrapping the bucket that will hold real state), set allow_ephemeral_state = True on the terraform_module. State is then kept between runs under bazel-out/<config>/bin/<pkg>/<name>.state/: private to the machine, forked per build configuration, and deleted by bazel clean. The runner prints the path after each run. Relative file arguments (-out=tfplan, -var-file=x.tfvars) resolve against the temp dir, so pass absolute paths. Because the aspect already installed the providers and the module manifest, the only thing a run-time terraform init still contributes is backend setup — so it runs only for subcommands that need one. version, fmt, validate, test and metadata skip it and work offline against a module with a remote backend; plan, apply and the rest initialize the backend as before. The practical consequences: a terraform_test on a module with a remote backend needs no credentials, and a configuration error in one of those subcommands is reported as itself rather than as a backend failure. terraform_validate_test, the validate aspect and terraform_test run the engine with the operator's CLI configuration disabled (TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE pointed at an empty file, CHECKPOINT_DISABLE=1, TF_IN_AUTOMATION=1), so a ~/.terraformrc on one machine cannot change what a check reports. bazel run keeps the full environment, since that is where credential helpers live.
6.title: Direct terraform CLI incompatibility

69.body: load("@rules_terraform//tofu:tofu_module.bzl", "tofu_module") tofu_module(name, deps, srcs, data, allow_ephemeral_state, lock) Defines a Terraform module that can be used as a dependency in other Terraform targets. ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this target. Name required deps Other terraform_module targets, a dependency hub (@<name> from a deps tag, or its //:providers / //:modules halves), individual @<name>//<namespace>_<name> providers, terraform_provider, or terraform_external_module targets this module depends on.A terraform_module dep is the Bazel half of a module block, the way a py_library dep is the Bazel half of an import: the .tf file names the path, deps says which target supplies it. A dep whose package already nests under this module's directory lands at that relative path; anything else is matched to a module block whose source ends with the dep's package name. List of labels optional [] srcs Terraform source files that make up this module: .tf, .tf.json, and OpenTofu's .tofu / .tofu.json.All of them must live directly in this target's package — a Terraform module is a single directory. Put nested .tf files in their own terraform_module and reference it with a module block. List of labels optional [] data Additional files or targets that should be available at runtime. List of labels optional [] allow_ephemeral_state Permit bazel run of apply, destroy and the other state-writing commands against a module with no backend or cloud block.Without a backend the engine keeps state in its working directory, which under Bazel is a staged copy that exists for one run. The runner therefore refuses those commands by default, naming the fix. With this set, state is kept under bazel-out between runs: private to the machine, forked per build configuration, and deleted by bazel clean. Set it only where losing the state is harmless: demos, sandboxes, or bootstrapping the bucket that will hold real state. Ignored when a backend is declared; plan and the read-only commands are never gated. Boolean optional False lock An optional .terraform.lock.hcl file. Label optional None

8.body: rules_terraform partitions external Terraform state into three buckets, each with its own resolution path and (where applicable) lock file. Every network fetch happens at repository-rule / bzlmod-extension time — build actions never touch the network. What Terraform actually sees at run time is a fully-populated module directory.

81.body:
No user-facing configuration. Mirrors //terraform:extensions.bzl%terraform_toolchains but resolves against //tofu:toolchain_type. Materializes @tofu_toolchains covering every supported OpenTofu version, each toolchain for the releases shipped in //tofu/private:versions.bzl and any a version tag requests, each guarded by a config_setting on //tofu/settings:version that the hub itself declares. rules_terraform's own MODULE.bazel registers the hub so downstream users get toolchain resolution for free. # Nothing to do beyond `bazel_dep` to use the newest shipped release.
bazel_dep(name = "rules_terraform", version = "...") # To use another release:
tofu_toolchains = use_extension("@rules_terraform//tofu:extensions.bzl", "tofu_toolchains")
tofu_toolchains.version(version = "1.9.1", default = True) tofu_toolchains.version takes the same version and default attributes as the Terraform extension's tag; see the Terraform page . For a tagged release the extension fetches that release's SHA256SUMS once and records the checksums as facts in MODULE.bazel.lock.
81.title: tofu_toolchains

82.body:
The tofu extension carries the same deps tag class as the terraform extension, defaulting to registry.opentofu.org. An OpenTofu-only repository uses it for everything and never loads //terraform:extensions.bzl: tofu = use_extension("@rules_terraform//tofu:extensions.bzl", "tofu")
tofu.deps( name = "app", lock = "//path/to/module:.terraform.lock.hcl", # written by tofu roots = ["//path/to/module:main.tf"],
)
use_repo(tofu, "app") The attributes are those documented for the terraform extension ; only the default registry differs. That default matters: registry.opentofu.org serves OpenTofu's own builds of the hashicorp/* providers, whose archive hashes differ from HashiCorp's, so a lock file written by tofu has to be resolved against it. Write the lock with the module's tofu_providers_lock updater and it will be. Each extension pools its own archives. A repository using both engines against the same dependencies should declare them through one extension rather than both, or the same archive is fetched twice.
82.breadcrumbs: OpenTofu Rules » extensions » Providers and modules
82.title: Providers and modules

83.body: Public build settings for //tofu. Each exported function is named after a build setting in this package and its docstring describes what the setting does. The function body returns the setting's label so callers can reference it programmatically. Picks which OpenTofu release the auto-registered toolchains resolve to. The tofu_toolchains extension declares one toolchain per (version, platform) for the releases shipped in //tofu/private:versions.bzl — the newest three when the table was generated — and for any release a tofu_toolchains.version(version = "…") tag asks for. For a tagged release the extension fetches the release's SHA256SUMS once and records the checksums as facts in MODULE.bazel.lock, so an older pin costs no change to rules_terraform and no network on later evaluations. Empty, the default, selects the extension's default: the release the root module marked version(…, default = True), else the newest shipped one. Any other value names one of the known releases. Set it globally in .bazelrc, per invocation via --@rules_terraform//tofu/settings:version=1.9.1, or per target with a Starlark configuration transition. The corresponding archive is fetched lazily on first use.
83.title: version
